editorial:
Imagine being a broke carpenter one day and waking up as a noble count the next. That is exactly what happens to Francesco in this funny story set in old Rome. You get to see him go from a simple life to dealing with the grumpy Prince Torquato and falling head over heels for the lovely Duchess Elisa. The movie has a light, breezy feel to it, focusing on the clash between a humble guy and a fancy, decaying upper class that has no idea how the real world works. It is a charming ride that pokes fun at the rich while keeping your heart warm.

You will really enjoy how the plot jumps from the streets of Rome to the battlefields of Libya, and finally across the ocean. The acting is spot on, making the comedy feel natural rather than forced. While the pacing slows down a bit in the middle, the payoff is totally worth it. If you are into old-school European comedies, you should definitely track this down. It would look great if you can find a 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection, but renting it on Apple TV is a great way to check it out first.
endingExplained: After seeing the horrors of war in Libya, Francesco decides he is done with the fake life of a nobleman. He realizes that money and titles do not bring happiness. He chooses to follow his true passion for singing instead. He and Duchess Elisa leave the bankrupt family legacy behind and sail to America together. They start a brand new life where Francesco can finally pursue his dream of becoming a star.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves fish-out-of-water stories and old European charm.
